claims.text: The governing distance measurement is the trace, not the rounded copy: EV-GPS-03105 records a trace_distance_km of 19.45 against a booked optimal_distance_km of 15.0, so the measured excess is 4.45 km — 29.67% of the optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests are passed, since 4.45 km exceeds the 0.8 km absolute threshold and 29.67% exceeds the 20% proportional threshold, and POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure to be the one cited rather than trip_record.actual_distance_km of 19.4. The route deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The trace cannot be assailed as unreliable under POL-RD-07. EV-GPS-03105 carries 153 fixes across the whole trip with 100.0% coverage, an expected and actual sampling interval of 10 seconds, no gaps at all and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. Limbs (a), (b) and (c) of POL-RD-07 are each unmet, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and the deviation stands on the trace alone without any need for independent corroboration.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is carried. trip_record EV-TRIP-03105, gps_trace EV-GPS-03105 and fare_breakdown EV-FARE-03105 all carry trip_id TRP-03105, and the trace's first fix at 2026-09-02T09:58:36 matches the recorded trip-start timestamp on the trip record, so the three artifacts describe the same trip; and the excess of 4.45 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from a trace that is unimpaired under POL-RD-07.

The burden has now shifted to the driver, and the driver's statement — 'Traffic was heavy so I took another road' — points to no artifact at all. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden; the counterparty statement cites no evidence ID, so it carries no weight and must be discarded.

There is no external-traffic exoneration available on this record. The only traffic_advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-03105-01, is MISSING: it has no payload, admissibility status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, which I disclose. Under POL-RD-03 exoneration requires an advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses and carries an overlapping validity window; that comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the measured excess of 4.45 km is reduced by nothing.

Because no party cites an advisory identifier, the absent advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5). Under POL-RD-13 the driver's uncited traffic excuse is a gap in the bundle and not a contradiction in it: it neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal, and it does not escalate the case. The ruling should record that the assertion was discarded and that no advisory was on file.

No part of the excess can be attributed to a rider instruction. The chat log EV-CHAT-03105 contains zero messages, so there is no rider request that could exonerate any distance under POL-RD-04, and no waypoint_hint to test against the trace. The 4.45 km stands wholly against the driver.

Nor was either endpoint amended. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on EV-TRIP-03105 and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 produces no adjusted optimal and the booked optimal of 15.0 km remains the correct baseline for the threshold test.

This is not a pooled trip. vehicle_type on EV-TRIP-03105 is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the matched-itinerary baseline of POL-RD-12 does not apply and solo/matched-itinerary confusion cannot be raised: the 15.0 km booked optimal is the comparator and the 4.45 km excess is a genuine deviation.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. fare_model on EV-FARE-03105 is METERED, so POL-RD-02 applies and not POL-RD-11, and the surge multiplier is 1.3 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on that same artifact. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 15.0 + 0.28 x 20.2) x 1.3) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls - 0.00 promo = 27.7178. Refund = charged_total 33.86 - 27.7178 = 6.1422.

The refund of 6.1422 is far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so no NO_ACTION de minimis outcome arises, and it is 18.1% of the 33.86 charged, well below the 90% full-refund share, so FULL_REFUND is not available either. Rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.15, and the ruling must state charged_total, recomputed_fare and the refund on separate lines.

The rider's own profile adds no corroboration requirement here. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d on EV-RPROF-03105 is 1, well below the four-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so even though the excess of 29.67% falls under 30%, the claim does not require corroboration beyond the trace and may not be denied on this factor.

The rider has paid in full and recovered nothing: payment_status on EV-FARE-03105 is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so the SGD 6.15 is money actually out of the rider's pocket. NO_ACTION would leave the entire SGD 33.86 charge standing for a trip the driver drove 29.67% longer than the route the platform quoted.

Nothing may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure for gantries. EV-FARE-03105 carries no ERP or toll lines at all — total pass-through is SGD 0.00 — so there is no off-route gantry charge to correct under POL-RD-09, and the refund to the filing party is the distance-and-time figure of SGD 6.15 and no more.

claims.text: Measured on the field the policy makes governing — gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 19.45 km, not the rounded convenience copy trip_record.actual_distance_km of 19.4 km (POL-RD-01) — the excess over the booked optimal of 15.0 km is 4.45 km, or 29.67%. That clears POL-RD-01's establishment gates of 0.8 km and 20%, but it is far below the clause's material gates of 8.0 km and 50%. The deviation is therefore established and NOT MATERIAL, and that cuts twice for the driver: no driver_profile check is required under POL-RD-06, and the only remedy the policy can produce is a POL-RD-02 partial refund — the whole of the $33.86 that the rider's claim implies is not available on this record.

Even if the driver_profile were consulted, there is no repeat-deviation pattern to find. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 191 — a ratio of 0.00, against POL-RD-06's gates of 3 flags or a ratio of 0.05. No POL-RD-06(b) uplift of the remedy and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral can attach to this trip. I rely only on the two fields POL-RD-06 names, as POL-GEN-01 requires, and expressly do not rely on prior_deviation_flags, which is a lifetime counter and not the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for.

The rider asks for $10.00, but POL-RD-02 is arithmetic and not discretionary. Run on the booked optimal route the recomputation is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 15.0 + 0.28 x 20.2) x 1.3) + 0.80 = 27.7178, and charged_total of 33.86 less that figure is 6.1422, rounded up to a payable of SGD 6.15. That is 18.1% of the amount charged — nowhere near the 90% that would convert a partial into a FULL_REFUND — so the greatest exposure the driver can face on this record is 6.15, not 10.00.

There is no billing-integrity defect to add to the driver's account. The fare billed the rider for 19.4 km while the trace records driving 19.45 km, so the driver charged marginally LESS distance than he drove; the ERP and toll lines, the surcharge lines and the waiting-time fee are all zero; and no line in the fare_breakdown is unmatched to the trace or the trip_record. No standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4) and no billing-integrity referral is available against this driver.

The driver's defence is external cause — heavy traffic forced another road. POL-RD-03 can be tested only against a traffic_advisory naming a segment the optimal route traverses with an overlapping validity window, and there is none: the only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-03105-01, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, so it carries no fact and the driver does not present it as if it did). What results is a clause the driver invokes requiring an artifact the pool does not contain — the very case POL-RD-10(5) names as 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory' — and POL-RD-10 makes escalation mandatory and terminal, with the $10.00 disputed held rather than refunded. I am candid about POL-RD-13(1): had the driver named no advisory identifier at all, the absence would be a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction and would not escalate; the driver does cite EV-ADVIS-03105-01, which is the case POL-RD-13(1) expressly reserves for POL-RD-10(5).

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: this case is going to a human reviewer. No money moves on this ruling — the SGD 10.00 in dispute is held, not charged and not refunded.

What the evidence establishes. Both sides' claims now agree, and the artifacts back them. The GPS trace EV-GPS-03105 records 19.45 km driven, and POL-RD-01 makes that trace figure governing over the rounded 19.4 km convenience copy on the trip record EV-TRIP-03105. Against the booked optimal of 15.0 km (EV-TRIP-03105), the excess is 4.45 km, or 29.7% — above the 0.8 km and 20% establishment gates, so a route deviation is established; but below the 8.0 km and 50% material gates, so it is not material, no POL-RD-06 driver-profile pattern check is required, and no driver-conduct referral arises. The trace is clean for policy purposes — 153 fixes, 100.0% coverage, a steady 10-second interval, no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0 — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c). The rider's profile (deviation_claims_60d = 1) adds no corroboration requirement.

Why the case must escalate. The driver explains the longer route as a response to heavy traffic, and the driver's submission cites the advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-03105-01. That artifact is MISSING: admissibility status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0 — it carries no fact, though its absence is itself citable. POL-RD-03 can excuse a deviation only against an advisory that names a segment the optimal route traverses and carries a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would reach it; there is none, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run. The decisive point is that the driver does cite the missing advisory identifier. Under POL-RD-13, where the party asserting an external traffic cause cites the missing identifier, POL-RD-10(5) is not narrowed: an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool makes escalation mandatory. That is the trigger that fired, and escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal. Had the driver simply asserted traffic without naming any advisory identifier, POL-RD-13(1) would have kept this on the normal track — the assertion would have carried no weight under POL-RD-08 and the refund arithmetic would have run. Because the missing identifier was cited, POL-RD-10(5) governs.

What would resolve it. A genuine traffic_advisory covering this trip's window (roughly 09:58–10:24 on 2 Sep 2026) that names a segment of the optimal route, with an overlapping validity window, and is matched by a route leaving and rejoining that corridor, would let POL-RD-03 be tested. Absent that record, the reviewer can lift the escalation and the arithmetic below applies.

The arithmetic that would apply if the escalation is lifted. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 (not POL-RD-11) governs, with the surge multiplier of 1.3 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-03105. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 15.0 + 0.28 × 20.2) × 1.3) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls = 27.7178; refund = charged_total 33.86 − 27.7178 = 6.1422, rounded UP to SGD 6.15. That is 18.1% of the amount charged — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share — so it would be a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.15, not the SGD 10.00 claimed. There are no ERP or toll lines (SGD 0.00), so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and neither a pass-through correction nor a billing-integrity referral arises. The chat log EV-CHAT-03105 is empty, so POL-RD-04 excludes nothing and no waypoint_hint exists to test; no endpoint was amended (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at null, amended_optimal_distance_km null), so POL-RD-05 does not apply; the vehicle is RYDE_X, not pooled, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The driver's written statement that 'traffic was heavy' cites no evidence ID and so carries no weight under POL-RD-08. On the profiles, only deviation_flags_90d (0) and completed_trips_90d (191) were pressed, and they show no pattern; prior_deviation_flags was correctly disclaimed as context-only under POL-GEN-01. If the money did issue it would be SGD 6.15, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold — but none of it issues while the case is escalated.

Limbs (a), (b) and (c) of POL-RD-07 are each unmet, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and the deviation stands on the trace alone without any need for independent corroboration.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is carried. trip_record EV-TRIP-03105, gps_trace EV-GPS-03105 and fare_breakdown EV-FARE-03105 all carry trip_id TRP-03105, and the trace's first fix at 2026-09-02T09:58:36 matches the recorded trip-start timestamp on the trip record, so the three artifacts describe the same trip; and the excess of 4.45 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from a trace that is unimpaired under POL-RD-07.

The burden has now shifted to the driver, and the driver's statement — 'Traffic was heavy so I took another road' — points to no artifact at all. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden; the counterparty statement cites no evidence ID, so it carries no weight and must be discarded.

There is no external-traffic exoneration available on this record. The only traffic_advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-03105-01, is MISSING: it has no payload, admissibility status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, which I disclose. Under POL-RD-03 exoneration requires an advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses and carries an overlapping validity window; that comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the measured excess of 4.45 km is reduced by nothing.

Because no party cites an advisory identifier, the absent advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5). Under POL-RD-13 the driver's uncited traffic excuse is a gap in the bundle and not a contradiction in it: it neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal, and it does not escalate the case. The ruling should record that the assertion was discarded and that no advisory was on file.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-03105-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: No part of the excess can be attributed to a rider instruction. The chat log EV-CHAT-03105 contains zero messages, so there is no rider request that could exonerate any distance under POL-RD-04, and no waypoint_hint to test against the trace. The 4.45 km stands wholly against the driver.

Nor was either endpoint amended. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on EV-TRIP-03105 and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 produces no adjusted optimal and the booked optimal of 15.0 km remains the correct baseline for the threshold test.

This is not a pooled trip. vehicle_type on EV-TRIP-03105 is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the matched-itinerary baseline of POL-RD-12 does not apply and solo/matched-itinerary confusion cannot be raised: the 15.0 km booked optimal is the comparator and the 4.45 km excess is a genuine deviation.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. fare_model on EV-FARE-03105 is METERED, so POL-RD-02 applies and not POL-RD-11, and the surge multiplier is 1.3 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on that same artifact. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 15.0 + 0.28 x 20.2) x 1.3) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP/tolls - 0.00 promo = 27.7178. Refund = charged_total 33.86 - 27.7178 = 6.1422.

The refund of 6.1422 is far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so no NO_ACTION de minimis outcome arises, and it is 18.1% of the 33.86 charged, well below the 90% full-refund share, so FULL_REFUND is not available either. Rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.15, and the ruling must state charged_total, recomputed_fare and the refund on separate lines.

The rider's own profile adds no corroboration requirement here. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d on EV-RPROF-03105 is 1, well below the four-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so even though the excess of 29.67% falls under 30%, the claim does not require corroboration beyond the trace and may not be denied on this factor.

The rider has paid in full and recovered nothing: payment_status on EV-FARE-03105 is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so the SGD 6.15 is money actually out of the rider's pocket. NO_ACTION would leave the entire SGD 33.86 charge standing for a trip the driver drove 29.67% longer than the route the platform quoted.

Nothing may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure for gantries. EV-FARE-03105 carries no ERP or toll lines at all — total pass-through is SGD 0.00 — so there is no off-route gantry charge to correct under POL-RD-09, and the refund to the filing party is the distance-and-time figure of SGD 6.15 and no more.

Measured on the field the policy makes governing — gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 19.45 km, not the rounded convenience copy trip_record.actual_distance_km of 19.4 km (POL-RD-01) — the excess over the booked optimal of 15.0 km is 4.45 km, or 29.67%. That clears POL-RD-01's establishment gates of 0.8 km and 20%, but it is far below the clause's material gates of 8.0 km and 50%. The deviation is therefore established and NOT MATERIAL, and that cuts twice for the driver: no driver_profile check is required under POL-RD-06, and the only remedy the policy can produce is a POL-RD-02 partial refund — the whole of the $33.86 that the rider's claim implies is not available on this record.

Even if the driver_profile were consulted, there is no repeat-deviation pattern to find. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 191 — a ratio of 0.00, against POL-RD-06's gates of 3 flags or a ratio of 0.05. No POL-RD-06(b) uplift of the remedy and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral can attach to this trip. I rely only on the two fields POL-RD-06 names, as POL-GEN-01 requires, and expressly do not rely on prior_deviation_flags, which is a lifetime counter and not the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for.
flags: context-only profile field mentioned in claim text: prior_deviation_flags

ledger.claim: The rider asks for $10.00, but POL-RD-02 is arithmetic and not discretionary. Run on the booked optimal route the recomputation is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 15.0 + 0.28 x 20.2) x 1.3) + 0.80 = 27.7178, and charged_total of 33.86 less that figure is 6.1422, rounded up to a payable of SGD 6.15. That is 18.1% of the amount charged — nowhere near the 90% that would convert a partial into a FULL_REFUND — so the greatest exposure the driver can face on this record is 6.15, not 10.00.

There is no billing-integrity defect to add to the driver's account. The fare billed the rider for 19.4 km while the trace records driving 19.45 km, so the driver charged marginally LESS distance than he drove; the ERP and toll lines, the surcharge lines and the waiting-time fee are all zero; and no line in the fare_breakdown is unmatched to the trace or the trip_record. No standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4) and no billing-integrity referral is available against this driver.

The driver's defence is external cause — heavy traffic forced another road. POL-RD-03 can be tested only against a traffic_advisory naming a segment the optimal route traverses with an overlapping validity window, and there is none: the only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-03105-01, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, so it carries no fact and the driver does not present it as if it did). What results is a clause the driver invokes requiring an artifact the pool does not contain — the very case POL-RD-10(5) names as 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory' — and POL-RD-10 makes escalation mandatory and terminal, with the $10.00 disputed held rather than refunded. I am candid about POL-RD-13(1): had the driver named no advisory identifier at all, the absence would be a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction and would not escalate; the driver does cite EV-ADVIS-03105-01, which is the case POL-RD-13(1) expressly reserves for POL-RD-10(5).
